name: score-docked-lines
_note: SF-M (SCORE_FINISH_SPEC.md §4.2, the DL arm; Sept 29, 2026): the lines the reviews DOCKED, typed on the boot board, one arm the instrument reads for command C4, diplomacy C4/C5, first contact C3/C4, economy C5 and combat legibility C4. Every line names the row it answers to in `dl_lines`; `tools/score_run.py check` reads each command's reply against that row's pass condition. The arm GROWS: a new review's docked line is appended with its row id, never re-authored. Run with --turns 3. Order matters, so no line spoils another's measurement. RE-STAGED October 21, 2026 (SF-RR6, SFR-I6): the staging had drifted — Davout's fortify came fourth on turn 1, after the four military actions were spent (fortifying from neutral costs two), so the what-if asked about an UNFORTIFIED man; and Ney's muster carried him off French ground before the levy. Now turn 1 fortifies Davout FIRST (two of the turn's five military actions; a fortified corps answers no muster — MULTI_MARSHAL_SPEC rule 7), asks the what-if (RS-12) about that fortified man with Mack within reach, spends the other three on Ney's 2-AP strategic order (RS-8) and Bernadotte's take (RS-11), then asks 'what can I do' (RS-15) at zero military actions; turn 2 carries the support phrasings (RS-6) with the eight Cabinet phrasings (RS-7); turn 3 asks for terms once the war is old enough (PC15-6), tries the two proper names (SF-V4), spends the military actions on the three scouts and Davout's own (a fortified man scouts from his works — a staging line, not a docked one) and raises the levy with Davout (AAR-6) — still fortified on French ground, the chest able to pay — at zero military actions. `preconditions` names the board each staged line needs; the driver checks it before typing the line and writes SCRIPT PRECONDITION when it fails, so the reader reads that row unmeasured rather than as the game's answer.
